problem:
The triangle $D$ has vertices $(2,2),(4,6),(6,2).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095768/assets/a4e507191aecd02e16fafba29598972df423e975dd554b260ca355f0cf6476a1.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 4=8.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=1\cdot 0-3\cdot (-2)=6.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,6\,|\cdot 8 \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$
